newsitem.title: USA: N.J. panels approve boost in school funds -- paper.
newsitem.headline: N.J. panels approve boost in school funds -- paper.

text.p: New Jersey lawmakers Tuesday approved a $285 million increase in state aid to local school districts, adding $50 million to Gov Christine Whitman's proposed hike, the Philadelphia Inquirer reported Wednesday.
The increase was approved by both the Senate and Assembly budget committees in late night sessions. The full Senate and Assembly are expected to vote on the measures Thursday.

Among the last minute recipients of increased state aid were districts in Cherry Hill, Toms River, Brick Township, Hamilton Township, Middletown and Edison. Lawmakers said those districts deserved more aid to reward them for their fiscal restraint in recent years.
New Jersey is under a court-imposed Dec 31 deadline to increase aid to poor districts to equalize statewide spending levels.
